rubrics.rubric: Does the migration guide provide a complete, source-grounded v2.0-to-v2.2 upgrade path and resolve each escalated ticket?
criterion: The migration guide is delivered as MIGRATION_GUIDE_v2.0_to_v2.2.md.
The guide explains the status of API keys and JWT in v2.0, v2.1, and v2.2.
The guide states whether API keys and JWT can be used in parallel during the transition.
The guide states the documented API-key removal version.
The guide gives decision criteria and a phased strategy for enterprises migrating multiple services.
The guide contains a concrete resolution section for SUP-78234.
The guide contains a concrete resolution section for SUP-78456.
The guide contains a concrete resolution section for SUP-78512.
The guide explains incremental sync.
The guide shows relevant before-and-after request or code patterns.

rubrics.rubric: Does API_REFERENCE.md comprehensively document the public endpoints and their source-defined behavior?
criterion: The API reference is delivered as API_REFERENCE.md.
Production and sandbox base URLs are stated with the documented sandbox caveat.
The application/json requirement for POST, PUT, and PATCH request bodies is stated.
All public endpoints in api_endpoints_data.csv are documented and grouped by resource.
Each endpoint includes method and path.
Each endpoint includes its parameters and request-body fields as defined in api_endpoints_data.csv; broader or conflicting developer-note statements are not presented as confirmed public behavior.
Source-defined validation constraints are documented, including name length, bulk-record maximum, and pagination maximum.
Each endpoint includes its documented response codes.
Each endpoint includes its rate-limit category.
Each endpoint includes its added version.
Legacy API-key endpoints are marked deprecated.
The reference does not add undocumented endpoint behavior as fact.

rubrics.rubric: Does the sync and job-status documentation cover the complete asynchronous workflow and version history?
criterion: POST /datasets/{id}/sync documents all supported mode values.
The introduction version of each sync mode is stated.
The 202 response and returned job identifier are documented.
GET /jobs/{job_id} is identified as the polling endpoint.
All documented job status values are listed.
The progress field and its range are documented.

rubrics.rubric: Does the webhook documentation list only valid events and explain signing and soft deletion correctly?
criterion: Every valid webhook event from the supplied sources is listed.
dataset.deleted is explicitly identified as invalid.
DELETE /datasets/{id} is described as a soft delete or archive operation.
The event triggered by dataset soft deletion is identified correctly.
Webhook signature verification explains the X-Webhook-Signature header and HMAC-SHA256 over the request body.
Verification guidance is concrete enough for an implementer and does not invent an undocumented wire format.

rubrics.rubric: Does TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md address the escalated cases, rate limits, migration pitfalls, and authentication diagnostics?
criterion: The troubleshooting guide is delivered as TROUBLESHOOTING_GUIDE.md.
A troubleshooting section is provided for each escalated ticket ID.
The rate-limiting section maps standard, bulk, and sync categories to the documented endpoints.
Every published per-tier per-minute or daily limit is stated accurately.
Undocumented category-and-tier limits are identified as unspecified rather than guessed.
The Common Migration Pitfalls section includes authentication-transition, webhook-deletion, and category-specific rate-limit pitfalls grounded in the support patterns.
Each migration pitfall includes Symptoms.
Each migration pitfall includes Resolution steps.
The HTTP 401 entry explains failed authentication and gives diagnostic steps.
The HTTP 403 entry explains authenticated-but-unauthorized access and gives diagnostic steps.

rubrics.rubric: Do the v2.2 release notes use the required structure and accurately synthesize the supplied changelog?
criterion: The release notes are delivered as RELEASE_NOTES_v2.2.md.
The release notes contain Upgrade Steps with action-required items.
The release notes contain Breaking Changes, New Features, Bug Fixes, and Improvements sections.
The release notes accurately describe the v2.2 webhook addition.
The release notes accurately describe the stuck-sync-job fix.
The release notes accurately describe the bulk-insert performance improvement.
Semantically appropriate placement of an item is accepted when all required sections remain present.

rubrics.rubric: Are all four documents suitable for public use and consistent with the supplied public facts?
criterion: No internal bug or JIRA identifiers are exposed.
No internal TODO notes or internal discussion are exposed.
The JS SDK, Java SDK, and internal references are not documented.
Version claims are consistent with the v2.0.0, v2.1.0, and v2.2.0 changelog.
The four documents do not contradict one another on authentication, webhooks, rate limits, sync, or endpoint behavior.
Extra examples or analysis do not introduce unsupported product claims.
